<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜># Image-ReID

This repository contains image-based person re-identification approaches proposed in these papers: 

- **[Spindle Net: Person Re-identification with Human Body Region Guided Feature Decomposition and Fusion](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.08335)** (Spotlight in CVPR 2017)
- **[Person Re-identification by Deep Learning Multi-scale Representations](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/8237638)** (ICIP 2017) 
- **[A new evaluation protocol for person re-identification](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.08134)** (arXiv)


## Dataset

Market-1501: A large-scale dataset for image-based person re-identification, which contains 

- 32,668 annotated bounding boxes of 1,501 identities 
- 6 images per identity on average, each identity is captured by at most 6 cameras
- Both hand-drawn bounding boxes and DPM-detected bounding boxes are provided
- The training set contains 12,936 images of 751 identities, the test set contains 19,732 images of 750 identities

For detailed description of the dataset, please refer to [Market-1501](https://www.quantum-machine.org/gdpr/data-sheets/Market-1501.pdf).

The original dataset can be downloaded from [here](http://www.liangzheng.org/Project/project_reid.html). The image files are in the format of `xxxx_cxsy.jpg`, where `xxxx` is the identity label, `cx` is the camera index, and `sy` is the DPM bounding box index.



### Pre-processing

The code expects the images to be placed in `data/market1501/images/`. Each identity should have its own sub-directory named with its label under `images/` (e.g. `data/market1501/images/0001/`).  This is only for convenience to group images of the same identity together. The images can have any filenames, but they must be in `.jpg` format.

The image filenames are in the format of `xxxx_cx_sy.jpg`, where `xxxx` is the identity label, `cx` is the camera index, and `sy` is the bounding box index. The image filenames are parsed to extract the identity label, camera index, and bounding box index. 

To pre-process the dataset, run `python3 prepare_market_1501.py`. This script will:

- Download the dataset if it does not exist
- Extract the images and place them in the correct directory structure
- Generate the training and testing splits

### Data Splits

The dataset is split into training and testing sets. The training set contains 12,936 images of 751 identities, and the testing set contains 19,732 images of 750 identities. The testing set is further split into query and gallery sets. The query set contains 3,368 images, and the gallery set contains 19,732 images (including the query images). The gallery set is used to search for the query images.

The data splits are defined in `data/market1501/splits.json`. The file contains the following keys:

- `train`: list of identity labels in the training set
- `query`: list of image filenames in the query set
- `gallery`: list of image filenames in the gallery set

### Data Loading

The data loading is handled by `data_loader.py`. The `Market1501` class is a PyTorch dataset that loads the images and their labels. The dataset can be used in two modes: `train` and `test`. In the `train` mode, the dataset returns the images and their identity labels. In the `test` mode, the dataset returns the images, their identity labels, and the camera indices.

The data loader also applies data augmentation to the training images, including random horizontal flipping, random cropping, and color jittering. The images are resized to 256x128 pixels before being fed into the network.

## Training

To train the Spindle Net model, run `python3 train.py`. The training script will:

- Load the training and testing data
- Initialize the model and the optimizer
- Train the model for a specified number of epochs
- Evaluate the model on the testing set after each epoch
- Save the model checkpoints

The training script accepts the following command-line arguments:

- `--data_dir`: path to the dataset directory (default: `data/market1501`)
- `--logs_dir`: path to the directory where the logs and model checkpoints will be saved (default: `logs`)
- `--batch_size`: batch size for training (default: 32)
- `--num_epochs`: number of training epochs (default: 50)
- `--lr`: learning rate (default: 0.1)
- `--step_size`: step size for learning rate scheduling (default: 20)
- `--gamma`: multiplicative factor of learning rate decay (default: 0.1)
- `--weight_decay`: weight decay (default: 5e-4)
- `--eval_freq`: frequency of evaluation (default: 1)
- `--save_freq`: frequency of saving model checkpoints (default: 10)

### Model

The Spindle Net model is defined in `model.py`. The model consists of three parts: 

- **Body Region Localization Network**: This network localizes the body regions (head, upper body, lower body) of the person. It is based on the ResNet-50 architecture, and the region localization is done by a spatial transformer network.

- **Feature Decomposition Network**: This network decomposes the features of the body regions into discriminative and non-discriminative parts. The discriminative parts are used for re-identification, and the non-discriminative parts are used for reconstruction.

- **Feature Fusion Network**: This network fuses the discriminative features of the body regions to form the final feature representation.

The model is trained with a combination of classification loss and reconstruction loss. The classification loss is the cross-entropy loss, and the reconstruction loss is the mean squared error loss.

### Evaluation

The model is evaluated on the testing set after each epoch. The evaluation metrics include the cumulative matching characteristic (CMC) curve and the mean average precision (mAP). The CMC curve is a plot of the recognition rate vs. the rank. The rank-1 recognition rate is the percentage of query images that are correctly matched with the top-1 gallery image. The mAP is the mean of the average precision over all the query images.

The evaluation is done by `evaluate.py`. The script computes the feature vectors of the query and gallery images, and then matches the query images with the gallery images using the cosine distance. The CMC curve and mAP are computed based on the matching results.

## Results

The Spindle Net model achieves the following results on the Market-1501 dataset:

- Rank-1 accuracy: 76.9%
- mAP: 56.4%

These results are comparable to the state-of-the-art methods at the time of publication.

## Conclusion

This repository provides an implementation of the Spindle Net model for person re-identification. The model uses a human body region guided feature decomposition and fusion approach to improve the discriminative power of the feature representation. The code is easy to use and can be adapted to other datasets and models.
